### 1. What "Sync to GitHub" means
When you "Commit" in your editor, you are only saving the changes **locally** (on your computer or in the temporary workspace). The "Sync" or "Push" step is what actually sends those saved changes to **GitHub.com**. 
*   **Why it matters:** Netlify is watching your GitHub repository. If you don't "Sync," Netlify doesn't know you made changes, so it won't update the website.
*   **How to do it:** In your IDE (like VS Code), usually after committing, the blue button changes to **"Sync Changes"** or **"Push"**. Click that to send the code to the web.

### 2. Why the page is blank on Netlify
Netlify is a static host. Browsers **cannot** read `.tsx` (TypeScript) files natively. If Netlify is just serving your files as-is, the browser sees `<script src="./index.tsx">` and doesn't know what to do with it, resulting in a blank page.
